title: Warnings, static checks and sanitizers
goal: Check the build, the instrumented run and the result against the contract as separate steps.

prerequisites.text: How a translation unit is built, why boundaries matter and where to read stderr.

terms.title: Compiler warning
terms.definition: A diagnostic emitted while checking the source. With -Werror, enabled warnings stop the build.

terms.title: Instrumented build
terms.definition: An executable with extra checks that run along the paths actually exercised.

terms.title: Contract check
terms.definition: A comparison of observed output and status against the expected result for one input.

sections.title: Three questions for one program
paragraphs: The compiler can spot an unused variable before running the program. With -Wall -Wextra, Clang reports unused variable. With -Werror, that source is rejected. This is a static check of the source.

In a native build, AddressSanitizer adds checks for memory accesses and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer checks supported undefined operations. They check the paths that actually run. Boundary tests separately check whether the result matches the contract.

sections.title: Use the declared count
paragraphs: In the safe example, count starts at 4 and printf uses it with %d. The control source declares skipped but passes a string literal to puts. Both have defined behaviour if compilation succeeds. The warning draws attention to the unused declaration.
steps: Read the example and run it without input. The output is count 4.
For the flag experiment, copy the skipped control source without its #pragma line. Clang reports a warning with -Wall -Wextra. Add -Werror to the same flags and compilation is rejected.
For native verification, try the command for the clean source in the next section. Record a runtime result only if the toolchain is available and the executable builds.
trace: unused variable for the skipped control

sections.title: Record each result in the right category
paragraphs: In a native Clang terminal, save the clean example as main.c and build it with clang -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=undefined main.c -o count-check. Run the resulting file (./count-check on POSIX, or .\count-check.exe on Windows if the build used that name). Check for count 4, empty stderr and status 0.

If the installed compiler or libraries do not support these flags, record environment unavailable and keep the actual build error. Code Studio uses Clang/WASI. Record its compile check separately from the native sanitizer run.
A program using count > 7 in place of count > 8 can run without a memory error. A contract test at 8 still exposes the wrong result.
The control uses #pragma clang diagnostic error to enable unused variable as an error for that source. This makes the rejection testable in Code Studio with the existing environment flags.

A sanitizer inserts checks during compilation. Whether a check triggers depends on the executed path. Code Studio uses the stated control runs here. An ordinary WASI result is not evidence of separate native instrumentation.

Record three observations independently. First, note whether the strict build produced an executable. Next, note whether this particular run was instrumented and whether it emitted reports. Finally, compare stdout against your predictions for the same inputs. An empty instrumentation log only shows that the checks reported no failure during that run.

sections.title: Keep three separate log entries
paragraphs: In practice, use limit as the actual upper boundary. Predict the output for 8. If a native toolchain is available, rerun 0, 8 and 9 with sanitizers and record those results separately. Keep the program's memory accesses within their valid lifetimes and bounds.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check the build, the instrumented run and the result against the contract as separate steps.

selfcheck.prompt: When does -Werror stop the skipped source?
feedback: Compilation rejects the unused variable diagnostic.
No input values are checked before the build succeeds.

selfcheck.prompt: The program rejects 8 without warnings or memory errors. Which check exposes the issue?
options: Contract test: input 8 must print count 8
feedback: The exact boundary exposes the incorrect rule.
A logic fault can have no compiler diagnostic.

selfcheck.prompt: What results would you log if a sanitizer run is unavailable in your environment?
selfcheck.feedback: Record the diagnostics build outcome and the exact inputs and results of the contract checks. Mark the instrumented run unavailable and keep the observed reason.

practice.title: Seat limit and separate checks
practice.task: Accept integers from 0 through 8. For a well-formed first line in range, print count and the number separated by a space. Print invalid for a rejected entry. Use limit as the sole upper bound, check a strict build if native Clang is available, and compare stdout for 0, 8 and 9.
criteria: Input 0 gives count 0, 8 gives count 8, and 9 gives invalid.
The condition uses limit as the single upper bound.
Log compilation, input results and the instrumented run or its unavailability separately.
practice.hint: Test the largest allowed input and its next neighbour first. Compare the condition with the declared limit. Would the condition still work if you changed only that one limit value?

steps.action: Run the starter with 8 using a regular build. If a strict build stopped earlier, read its diagnostic separately.
steps.why: Distinguish the unused declaration from the incorrect threshold.
steps.expected: A regular run writes invalid. Strict Clang reports unused variable for limit.

steps.action: Replace 7 with limit and run 0, 8 and 9.
steps.why: Check the inclusive boundary and its neighbours.
steps.expected: The separate runs produce count 0, count 8 and invalid.

steps.action: If native Clang is available, build the safe fixed version with sanitizers and repeat the same inputs.
steps.why: Record observed stdout, stderr and exit statuses separately from build diagnostics.
steps.expected: On a successful instrumented run, stdout matches, stderr is empty and status is 0. If the toolchain lacks support, record the observed environment failure.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: In a separate copy, set limit to 12. Choose a boundary value, an outside value and malformed input to distinguish range checking from parsing.
criteria: 12 gives count 12; 13 and 12x give invalid for different reasons.

teaching.scene: A counter builds without visible warnings. Check three different things: its format arguments, whether a runtime problem can be observed, and what it does at the largest allowed value.

predict.prompt: The example has an int named count with value 4. What does %d receive, and what result can you observe? Can that run verify the limit of 8 in a different task?
predict.answer: The %d conversion receives the expected int and stdout contains count 4. The run checks that call. A limit in the practice task needs separate input cases.

apply.prompt: You are checking the corrected counter. The strict build passed, but a sanitizer run is unavailable. Input 8 produced count 8 and 9 produced invalid. What findings belong in the report?
apply.answer: The strict build passed. The two lines match the contract at the upper boundary and just beyond it. Record why instrumentation was unavailable. There is no result from an instrumented run.

practice.strategy: Write the exact outputs for 0, 8, and 9. Find where the limit is declared and where the program actually checks the number. If native Clang is available, add a strict build.
practice.diagnosis: An unused limit may cause a warning, but deleting it would leave the wrong boundary. Check that the comparison uses the intended limit and produces different outcomes for 8 and 9.

syntax.explanation: A printf conversion and the actual argument type must agree. The compiler can often check them when the format is a string literal and the function declaration is visible.
syntax.mistake: Fix a format-type warning before running the modified code. A warning-free build still needs a contract check at the input boundary.
